title: Wild kernel of the action on initial forms of a Galois valued extension
statement:
Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute value: $|x|=0$ iff $x=0$, $|xy|=|x||y|$, $|1|=1$, $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$, and $|a|\notin\{0,1\}$ for some $a$. All finite extensions carry an extending absolute value. For each such field $F$ set $F^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\mathfrak m_F=\{x:|x|<1\}$, $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\mathfrak m_F$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|$. Write $e(F/E)=[\Gamma_F:\Gamma_E]$, $f(F/E)=[\widetilde F:\widetilde E]$, and let $p=\operatorname{char}(\widetilde K)$. A finite field extension is separable when every minimal polynomial has distinct roots. Every finite separable extension $L/K$ is contained in a finite Galois extension $N/K$, i.e. separable and normal, where normal means that the minimal polynomial over $K$ of every element of $N$ splits into linear factors in $N[T]$. For any finite Galois $N/K$, put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(N)$ and
$$P=\{\sigma\in G: |\sigma(x)-x|<|x|\text{ for every }x\in N^\times\},\qquad T=N^P=\{x\in N:\forall\sigma\in P,\ \sigma(x)=x\}.$$
Then $P$ is normal in $G$. If $p>0$, its order is a power of $p$; if $p=0$, it is trivial. The field $T$ has separable residue extension over $K$, $e(T/K)$ is prime to $p$ when $p>0$, and $[T:K]=e(T/K)f(T/K)$. Moreover $N/T$ has purely inseparable residue extension, meaning every residue element has a $p$-power in $\widetilde T$ when $p>0$ and the residue fields are equal when $p=0$; $e(N/T)$ and $f(N/T)$ are powers of $p$ when $p>0$ and both are one when $p=0$. No discreteness or perfection of the residue field is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the finite-Galois-envelope node to the one extension $L/K$; its embedding is injective, so identify $L$ with its image in $N$. The extending absolute value on $N$ is available by hypothesis. For every $\sigma\in G$, $x\mapsto|\sigma(x)|$ is another extending absolute value, hence equals $|x|$ by uniqueness. The finite-Galois fixed-field node makes $G$ finite. The defining inequalities show directly that $P$ is a subgroup: $(\sigma\tau)x-x=\sigma(\tau x-x)+(\sigma x-x)$; for inverses apply the inequality to $\sigma^{-1}x$. For $g\in G$, $|(g\sigma g^{-1})x-x|=|\sigma(g^{-1}x)-g^{-1}x|<|g^{-1}x|=|x|$. Thus $P$ is normal.

source.place: Section 6.2.8, pairing (6.2.9), and Proposition 6.2.12, final averaging argument; sixth release at the author site, PDF pp.209–211, printed pp.207–209. Local archival copy WANTED; online text read.

proof.text: If $q$ is prime and $q\ne p$ (any prime if $p=0$), then $|q|=1$: the image of $q$ in the residue field is nonzero. Suppose $\sigma\in P$ has order $q$. Put $A(y)=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}\sigma^i(y)$. For nonzero $y$, each $\sigma^i(y)-y$ has norm less than $|y|$, so $|A(y)-qy|<|y|=|qy|$ and therefore $|A(y)|=|y|$. Hence $A$ is injective. But $A(z-\sigma z)=z-\sigma^qz=0$, forcing $\sigma z=z$ for every $z$, a contradiction. Cauchy's theorem, applied to the finite subgroup $P$ of $K$-automorphisms of $N$, now excludes every prime divisor of $|P|$ except $p$. By prime factorization $m:=|P|$ is $p^a$ for some $a\ge0$ if $p>0$. If $p=0$, it has no prime divisor, so $m=1$ and $P=1$.

proof.text:
For $x\in N^\times$ define $b(x)=\prod_{\rho\in P}\rho(x)$. The factors are permuted by $P$, so $b(x)\in T^\times$. Write each factor as $x(1+\epsilon_\rho)$ with $|\epsilon_\rho|<1$. Expanding the finite product gives
$$|b(x)-x^m|<|x|^m,\qquad |b(x)|=|x|^m.$$
This is just a finite product of terms congruent to $1$ modulo the maximal ideal. For a unit $x$ it also gives $\overline{b(x)}=\bar x^m$. Zero residue elements satisfy the same power-membership assertion trivially.

source.place: Section 6.2.8, pairing (6.2.9), and Proposition 6.2.12, final averaging argument; sixth release at the author site, PDF pp.209–211, printed pp.207–209. Local archival copy WANTED; online text read.

proof.text: The degree bound for $N/T$ makes $\Gamma_N/\Gamma_T$ finite and $\widetilde N/\widetilde T$ finite. Since $|b(x)|=|x|^m$, every element of the value-group quotient has $m$-th power $1$. For $p>0$, $m=p^a$, so the finite-group prime-power cardinality leaf gives $e(N/T)=p^c$. Every nonzero residue element of $N$ has a unit representative, and the preceding product gives its $p^a$-th power in $\widetilde T$; hence the residue extension is purely inseparable. The purely inseparable root-tower node gives a tower of degree-$p$ steps, so $f(N/T)$ is also a power of $p$ (the empty tower has degree one). For $p=0$, step 2 gives $P=1$, hence $T=N$; the upper value groups and residue fields are equal.

proof.text: The normal-fixed-quotient node applied to $P\triangleleft G$ shows that $T/K$ is finite Galois and that restriction identifies $G/P$ with $H:=\operatorname{Aut}_K(T)$. Thus every $\tau\in H$ lifts to a $\sigma\in G$. The finite-Galois fixed-field node, now applied to $T/K$, gives $|H|=[T:K]$. Every element of $H$ is an isometry, since it is a restriction of such a $\sigma$.

source.place: Section 6.2.8, pairing (6.2.9), and Proposition 6.2.12, final averaging argument; sixth release at the author site, PDF pp.209–211, printed pp.207–209. Local archival copy WANTED; online text read.

proof.text:
Let $\tau\in H$ act trivially on all initial forms of $T$, that is $|\tau(t)-t|<|t|$ for every $t\ne0$ in $T$, and lift it to $\sigma\in G$ using the restriction isomorphism. For $x\in N^\times$ the inequalities of step 3, their images under the isometry $\sigma$, and $|\sigma(b(x))-b(x)|<|b(x)|$ give
$$|(\sigma x)^m-x^m|<|x|^m.$$
The unit $u=\sigma x/x$ therefore satisfies $\bar u^m=1$ in $\widetilde N$. If $p>0$, then $m=p^a$ and $(\bar u-1)^{p^a}=\bar u^{p^a}-1=0$, so $\bar u=1$ since a field has no nonzero nilpotent. If $p=0$, $m=1$ gives the same conclusion directly. Thus $|\sigma x-x|<|x|$ for all $x\ne0$, so $\sigma\in P$. Its restriction to $T$ is the identity. This proves that the initial-form kernel of $H$ is trivial.

source.place: Section 6.2.8, pairing (6.2.9), and Proposition 6.2.12, final averaging argument; sixth release at the author site, PDF pp.209–211, printed pp.207–209. Local archival copy WANTED; online text read.

proof.text:
Apply the initial-form automorphism bound with $E=T,F=K$ and $H=\operatorname{Aut}_K(T)$. Its finiteness hypotheses on $e,f$ follow from the valued-extension degree bound. Its kernel is trivial by step 6. Write $e=e(T/K)$, $f=f(T/K)$ and use $e',s$ as in that bound. Combining it with the degree bound and step 5 yields
$$ef\le[T:K]=|H|\le e's\le ef.$$
Since $e,f,e',s$ are positive integers with $e'\le e$ and $s\le f$, equality forces $e'=e$ and $s=f$. The bound's separability criterion now makes $\widetilde T/\widetilde K$ separable, $e'=e$ makes $e$ prime to $p$ when $p>0$, and equality gives $[T:K]=ef$. For $p=0$ the convention $e'=e$ imposes no index restriction, as required.
